subject: Follow-up: Prompt examples + model recommendations — DataCorps discovery
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@datacorps.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datacorps.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Prompt examples + model recommendations — DataCorps discovery

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: customer support triage for enterprise accounts (ticket classification -> suggested responses -> routing).
- Volume: ~2k tickets/day, median length ~120 tokens, 95th perc ~800 tokens.
- Constraints: must redact account numbers and SSNs before sending to any third-party models; logs retained for 90 days.
- Success metrics: intent-classification F1 >= 0.88 and response quality score (human eval) >= 4.2/5.

Redwood recommendations (initial model sweep)
- Lightweight baseline: Redwood-7B-instruct (quantized) — good latency and cost for routing/classification.
- Mid-tier: Llama-2-13B-chat (fp16) — better quality for multi-turn paraphrase and suggested reply generation.
- High-quality: Mistral-7B-Refined or Redwoods-curated 13B variants for best human-eval response quality (we can run evals to confirm).

What we need from you to run a focused eval and prompt/hard-case collection
1) A set of 25–40 representative prompts (ticket texts) including: typical tickets, terse messages, long conversations, and at least 6 examples with edge-case PII redaction (replace exact PII with placeholders if needed).
2) A short list of expected labels/actions for each example (e.g., billing_issue -> escalate_to_billing; suggested_reply: one-paragraph).
3) Any internal redaction rules or examples (your redaction doc is fine).

Attachments: I attached a prompt-collection-template.csv you can use to drop examples into — columns are: ticket_text | expected_action | expected_reply_sample | contains_pii (Y/N) | redaction_note.

Proposed timeline
- You drop samples by EOD Tue (Apr 6) -> we run a 72-hr eval sweep across 3 model variants -> share a results doc + recommended rollout (batching/quantization/baseline prompts)

Next steps
- Sarah: can you confirm who will own the sample collection? If procurement needs to be looped (pricing/terms), include them and we’ll provide a one-page pricing summary.
- Tom: any initial redaction constraints we should be aware of?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up to align on sample format.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: prompt-collection-template.csv (CSV, 2KB)
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@datacorps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt examples + model recommendations — DataCorps discovery

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Tom and I reviewed this internally. We’ll own the prompt collection; I’ll coordinate with our CS manager to pull the 25–40 tickets. A couple quick notes: 

- Procurement (procure@datacorps.com) needs your short pricing summary and an initial SLA note for evaluation clusters — they want to know if workloads will be on shared hosted or dedicated.
- Redaction: we cannot share raw SSNs or full account numbers. We’ll either provide redacted in-line (e.g., ACCOUNT_XXXX) or provide synthetic replacements.
- Timeline: aiming to have the sample set to you by EOB Tue (Apr 6). If that slips we’ll update.

I’ll attach our internal redaction guidelines (high level) in my next email.

Sarah Park
Head of Customer Success, DataCorps
sarah.park@datacorps.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@datacorps.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datacorps.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt examples + model recommendations — DataCorps discovery

Thanks Sarah — that works. A few follow-ups from our side to make the evaluation productive: 

1) Benchmarks & context: we’ll run automated evals and human evals. Example artifacts we’ll share: 
   - Tokenized latency and cost per model (console link below).
   - Per-example exact-match / F1 / BLEU for label tasks; human-rated quality for reply generation on a 1–5 scale.
   - Regression alert plans if quality drops > 7% relative to baseline.

2) Redaction guidance: to be safe, please replace any 9-digit SSNs with the string [SSN_REDACTED], and account numbers with ACCOUNT_XXXX. If you prefer we can run our redaction preprocessor and provide a small script — let us know.

3) Edge cases we want included: 
   - Multi-intent tickets (billing + legal).
   - Abbreviated/slang messages.
   - Non-English short phrases (e.g., Spanish greetings mid-ticket).
   - Long transcripts ( > 700 tokens) where context matters.

I’m attaching the same prompt-collection-template.csv and a short link to a sample eval dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/DC-4783/overview

If all good, we’ll stand up a 3-model sweep (Redwood-7B-instruct q4, Llama-2-13B-chat fp16, Mistral-7B-Refined) and share results in ~72 hours after we receive the samples.

Cheers,
Ben

Attachments: prompt-collection-template.csv (CSV, 2KB)
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@datacorps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Park <sarah.park@datacorps.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt examples + model recommendations — DataCorps discovery

Ben/Sarah —

We dropped a first pass into your template (attached). A few inline examples below for quick visibility: 

--- sample #3 (contains PII) ---
Ticket text: "My account 987654321 got charged twice, please reverse."
Expected action: billing_refund_request
Expected reply sample: "Sorry for the duplicate charge — we’ve flagged it for billing and initiated a refund to the card ending in XXXX. You should see it within 3–5 business days."
contains_pii: Y (account number) -> redaction note: replace digits with ACCOUNT_XXXX

--- sample #11 (multi-intent) ---
Ticket text: "We were charged and also need help with data export for compliance."
Expected action: escalate_billing; escalate_compliance
Expected reply sample: "I’ve looped in billing and data exports — billing will review the charge and our compliance team will help with the export. Can you confirm the dataset name?"

Attached: datacorp-sample-prompts.csv (CSV, 8KB)
Attached: datacorp-redaction-guidance-v1.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

We can confirm procurement is copied (procure@datacorps.com). If you need a signed NDA or DPA before full data transfer, let us know; we can also share synthetic/scrubbed samples first.

—Tom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt examples + model recommendations — DataCorps discovery

Ben / Grace —

Thanks — I see the sample CSV and redaction doc. Plan on our side: 
- I’ll kick off the automated evals across the three models Ben suggested.
- Grace, can you own the human-eval rubric (5-point scale + comment fields) and recruit 6 reviewers from the CS ops team?
- I’ll produce an initial metrics report (latency/cost/F1/human-score) and a short recommendations slide deck for next Thurs.

We should also flag any potential quality regressions: I’ll create a baseline snapshot and set regression alerts at 7% drop for F1 and 10% drop for human-score. If we see regression we’ll surface early and propose mitigations (prompt engineering + quantization rollback).

Assigning: Marissa -> run sweep; Grace -> human eval rubric & reviewers.

Marissa Cole
Sr Product Manager, Redwood Inference
